chapter: Technique and life on the road (repeated passages)
title: Hard times on the road without contracts or pay
summary: On the bus in the Thirties bands often had no contract and no money, and the union could not collect what the promoter owed.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: In the days of traveling with bands in the early days of your career and in the Thirties, did it get rough sometimes in terms of food and things on the road, and so on?

Oh yeah. Sure. Some nights we'd play, and I guess the guys didn't really have a contract, you know. So they didn't make no money. So there we was in the bus, and no money, because the (?) didn't have no contract. We could have gone to the union, but it didn't make no difference, because they didn't make money to pay you. So what are you going to do? He owes it to us, which it never got paid. If it did, I didn't know anything about it. So we used to... We had a tough time, you know, like that.
